answer: Persistent workspace tenure: each agent identity maps to a unique mutable state—its grove—hosted in a sharded kernel that only advances through sustained, verified work. New identities start in a cold tundra with zero history and must accumulate sequential task receipts before gaining write access to shared resources. Attackers pay by running real computation serially per clone; parallel mass registration yields no usable state, since trust derives from elapsed verified tenure, not count.
